ATAC fragments, peak calling and recount

Source: vignettes/atac-fragments-workflow.Rmd
atac-fragments-workflow.Rmd

Inputs and interpretation

This external-data recipe extends the common-matrix workflow. Use the same hg38 PBMC cells, explicitly prepared fragments/index and Ensembl 98 transcript annotation. The acceptance run restricts both reference and fragments to chr1. Therefore its FRiP, TSS summaries, peaks and coverage describe that retained region, not genome-wide QC. Full-genome use requires corresponding full-genome resources and a suitable effective genome size.

Prepare the 10x fragments and index and Ensembl 98 GTF explicitly. Preserve original files and checksums. Restrict fragments by chromosome and the exact selected barcodes; preserve records and their existing fifth column. Do not strip barcode suffixes. The GTF uses chromosome 1; explicitly rename that selected sequence to chr1 for this known reference before attaching it. SCOP itself does not guess chromosome styles or reference assemblies.

data_dir <- "atac_data"
atac <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "atac_counts.rds"))
prefix <- "10k_pbmc_ATACv2_nextgem_Chromium_Controller_"
base <- paste0("https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/2.1.0/",
  "10k_pbmc_ATACv2_nextgem_Chromium_Controller/")
source_fragments <- file.path(data_dir, paste0(prefix, "fragments.tsv.gz"))
utils::download.file(paste0(base, basename(source_fragments)), source_fragments, mode = "wb")
select_fragments <- function(source, target, cells) {
  stopifnot(!file.exists(target))
  input <- gzfile(source, "rt")
  output <- file(target, "wt")
  on.exit({ close(input); close(output) })
  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(input, n = 100000, warn = FALSE)
    if (!length(lines)) break
    lines <- lines[!startsWith(lines, "#")]
    fields <- strsplit(lines, "\t", fixed = TRUE)
    keep <- vapply(fields, function(x) x[[1]] == "chr1" && x[[4]] %in% cells, logical(1))
    writeLines(lines[keep], output)
  }
}
select_fragments(source_fragments, file.path(data_dir, "pbmc-chr1-selected.tsv"), colnames(atac))
gtf <- file.path(data_dir, "Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.98.gtf.gz")
utils::download.file(
  "https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/release-98/gtf/homo_sapiens/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.98.gtf.gz",
  gtf, mode = "wb")
annotation <- rtracklayer::import(gtf)
annotation <- GenomeInfoDb::keepSeqlevels(annotation, "1", pruning.mode = "coarse")
GenomeInfoDb::seqlevels(annotation) <- "chr1"
annotation <- annotation[annotation$type %in% c("transcript", "exon")]
annotation$tx_id <- annotation$transcript_id
GenomeInfoDb::genome(annotation) <- "hg38"
atac <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "atac_counts.rds"))
# This prepared file contains genuine chr1 records for the selected cells.
plain <- file.path(data_dir, "pbmc-chr1-selected.tsv")
fragment_file <- Rsamtools::bgzip(plain, dest = paste0(plain, ".gz"))
Rsamtools::indexTabix(fragment_file, format = "bed")
fragment <- Signac::CreateFragmentObject(fragment_file,
  cells = stats::setNames(colnames(atac), colnames(atac)))
Signac::Fragments(atac[["peaks"]]) <- fragment
Signac::Annotation(atac[["peaks"]]) <- annotation
stopifnot(scop::CheckATACData(atac)$fragments_ready)

QC and capture-specific doublets 

atac <- scop::RunATACQC(atac, assay = "peaks", frip = TRUE)
summary(atac$frip)
atac <- scop::RunDoubletCalling(atac, assay = "peaks", sample.by = "capture",
  db_rate = 0.08, seed = 17)
table(atac$db.scDblFinder_class)
saveRDS(atac, "pbmc_before_doublet_filter.rds")
selected <- colnames(atac)[atac$db.scDblFinder_class == "singlet"]
atac <- subset(atac, cells = selected)

Direct FRiP counts fragment records once over the peak union, even when a record overlaps multiple peaks. It does not sum the fifth-column read support. Recount may count one record in several overlapping features, so its column sum is not a general FRiP numerator. Requested filters fail if their metrics are unavailable.

For ATAC, scDblFinder uses feature aggregation and normFeatures, independently within declared captures. The default ATAC expected rate is the backend’s per-capture rate; this example explicitly supplies 0.08. Choose this value from capture chemistry and loading, not the desired number of removed cells. Existing upstream doublet calls can instead be used directly. The worked run predicted 109 doublets and retained 891 cells; these predictions are not verified labels.

MACS2, consensus and sequence scanning before recount

Prepare MACS2 2.2.9.1 separately. The accepted run used a Linux Docker image built from official MACS2 source, Python 3.10, NumPy 1.26.4 and Cython 0.29.37. Signac 1.16.0 performs splitting in the R host. An explicitly configured executable launcher may invoke the pinned container with known mounted paths; SCOP does not install containers, translate paths or choose an alternative caller.

macs2_path <- "macs2" # A command on PATH, executable path, or configured container launcher.
reference <- Rsamtools::FaFile(file.path(data_dir, "hg38-chr1.fa"))
pfm <- TFBSTools::getMatrixSet(JASPAR2020::JASPAR2020, opts = list(
  ID = c("MA0139.1", "MA0080.5", "MA0105.4", "MA0107.1", "MA0039.4", "MA0466.2", "MA0098.3")))
effective_size <- sum(Biostrings::letterFrequency(
  Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(file.path(data_dir, "hg38-chr1.fa")),
  c("A", "C", "G", "T")))
called <- scop::CallATACPeaks(atac, sample.by = "capture",
  macs2.path = macs2_path, outdir = "pbmc_peak_calls",
  effective.genome.size = effective_size)
called$groups
lengths(called$peaks)
common <- scop::CombineATACPeaks(called$peaks, genome = "hg38")
scanned <- scop::AddATACMotifs(common$ranges, reference, pfm, genome.id = "hg38")

For the chromosome-scoped example, the effective size is the number of A/C/G/T bases in the retained reference. This is an explicit reference-length choice, not a genome-wide mappability estimate. Peak significance is not a condition comparison with biological replication. In the acceptance run MACS2 retained 8,108 peaks. Each call keeps split BEDs, exact arguments, stdout/stderr, exit status and native outputs. A failed process cannot become a successful empty result. A successful empty narrowPeak file remains an empty set.

If a call fails, inspect its .log and commands.rds in the output directory. receipt.rds and groups.rds retain the selected cells, capture/group mapping and source fragments even after an error. Correct the cause and use a new output directory for the next call; an existing result is never overwritten.

With multiple captures, calls remain separate. An optional group.by subdivides captures. CombineATACPeaks(groups = ..., min.support = ...) applies support within declared groups before taking their union. Its support counts input sets contributing to connected intervals, not support at every base. Sequence scanning above uses ranges, DNA and PWMs without placeholder counts.

Recount and final representation 

final <- scop::RecountATAC(atac, common$ranges, new.assay = "ATACFinal")
stopifnot(identical(rownames(final[["ATACFinal"]]), scanned$receipt$peaks))
Signac::Motifs(final[["ATACFinal"]]) <- scanned$motifs
final[["ATACFinal"]] <- SeuratObject::AddMetaData(final[["ATACFinal"]], scanned$statistics)
Signac::Annotation(final[["ATACFinal"]]) <- annotation
final <- scop::RunStandardWorkflow(final, assay = "ATACFinal", prefix = "ATACFinal",
  nHVF = 5000, linear_reduction_dims = 25, linear_reduction_dims_use = 2:20,
  cores = 1)

Native Signac FeatureMatrix computes the new counts. Recount creates a new assay and does not copy old normalized data, reductions, motifs or links into it. Here the sequence annotation is explicitly attached only after verifying the same peak order. Inspect final depth correlations again; initial dimensions are not automatically appropriate after changing the feature universe.

Gene activity, chromVAR, coverage and reload 

final <- scop::RunGeneActivity(final, assay = "ATACFinal",
  features = c("C1QA", "C1QB", "C1QC", "FCGR1A", "IL6R", "CD247",
    "RGS1", "SELL", "JUN", "CTSS", "CD53"))
final <- scop::RunChromVAR(final, reference, genome.id = "hg38", assay = "ATACFinal",
  new.assay = "chromvarFinal", niterations = 25, seed = 19)
scop::CoverageTrackPlot(final, region = "chr1-22650000-22700000",
  assay = "ATACFinal", group.by = "ATACFinallsiclusters")
scop::ExportATACResults(final, outdir = "pbmc_fragments_export", assay = "ATACFinal", counts = TRUE)
# In a fresh R session:
restored <- readRDS("pbmc_fragments_export/object.rds")
scop::CheckATACData(restored, assay = "ATACFinal")

Gene activity is fragment accessibility over annotated gene bodies/promoters, not measured RNA. Coverage is a descriptive locus view. Saved objects retain external file references; missing fragments block fragment-dependent steps but do not invalidate matrix-only analyses. Relocate files explicitly with Signac’s verified path-update API. For condition inference, use biological replicates as in the paired DAR workflow.
